_note: CARGO RUN, REMOTE TO REMOTE, ON THE BOARD. His 2026-10-14 14:33: 'thinking we should have a cargo run mission,
remote to remote. Talking on both ends', then 14:53 'it'll be both types eventually, but let's start missionboard'
and 'This is peak dad game'. Design and words are Jessica's.
The shape is 15a's (talk, pickup, talk; a hand-back talk takes the cargo, as 11a's), with a planet jump between
the two talks. The two ends know each other and the player is the only thing travelling between them: each
tells you something about the other, and the far end answers what the near end said.
THE LINT FAILS ON PURPOSE: this is the request to Eliza, as 10a's red lint was. The board template today takes
fights only (defeat, clear, hold), one place, and no <SecondPlace> or <SecondPlanet> token. This needs: talk and
pickup on the board, a second place that is its own remote request (another planet), and the two tokens. The
same second-place work unblocks 10a. How 'second' is spelled on a board recipe is hers; written here as on beats.
Pay: med on the hand-back (it crosses planets, README rule 3).

pickup on MB26 and MB27, so not new to the mod. Not on the Delve approved list yet. Small, about half a metre.

prose.name: Hauling: Engineer's Toolbox to <SecondPlanet>
prose.briefing: A retiring engineer at the <Place> wants her toolbox taken to the apprentice she trained, who runs his own site at the <SecondPlace> now.
prose.card: Delivery Contract. Deliver a toolbox from the <Place>, <Planet> to the <SecondPlace>, <SecondPlanet>. Payment on delivery.

beats.objective: Talk to the engineer at the <Place>
beats.journal: The retiring engineer wants her toolbox to go to the apprentice she trained, who she says will pretend he doesn't need it. I need to collect it and take it to him.
greeting: You're the hauler? I'm retiring, and my toolbox goes to the lad I trained. The big wrench in it was my mother's.

reply: He runs his own site now, off-world. The box is just there. Don't let him tell you he doesn't need it.

exchanges.prompt: A wrench that old should be on a wall.
reply: You'd know. Nobody makes steel like that any more. It's for using, though. Walls are for people who've stopped.
Because I'm done. Forty years of fixing other people's mistakes. My knees decided before I did.
Every tool I ever trusted. Half of them I made. Tell him to mind the wrench.

beats._talk: Exchange 0 closes the talk and sets this beat's stage; the rest loop back in any order. Voice is ElevenLabs' 'Lily, Velvety Actress' (British, middle aged). 2026-10-14 16:2x, his catch: the menu is any order, so the greeting now says she is retiring and he was her apprentice, and every prompt is askable cold.

beats.journal: I've got the toolbox. Every tool in it has been cleaned and oiled, and the big wrench is wrapped in a cloth on its own. Now I need to take it to the apprentice.
beats.name: Engineer's Toolbox

beats.objective: Deliver the toolbox to the apprentice at the <SecondPlace>
beats.journal: I delivered the toolbox to her apprentice. He said he'd call her tonight.

person.name: Kit Navarro
hellos: Can I help? Sorry, it's a mess.

greeting: That's her box. She actually sent it.

exchanges.prompt: She wanted you to have it.
reply: She told me I'd never be ready for this box. I'll call her tonight.

exchanges.prompt: First site of your own. Scared?
reply: Every morning. She told me the day I stop being scared is the day I start breaking things.

exchanges.prompt: She said you'd pretend you didn't need it.
reply: Ha. I've been borrowing a wrench off the cook for a month. Don't tell her that.

beats._talk: The HAND-BACK: the whole last step, so its stage is 100 and it takes the toolbox. Each prompt answers something she said at the first site. Voice is ElevenLabs' 'Hunter' (Canadian, chill, young). 2026-10-14 16:2x: the last prompt was 'She said you asked why about everything', which is only true if the player asked her an optional question; now askable cold, and it still echoes her line if they did. 'She said you'd pretend' stays: it comes from her closing reply, which every player hears.
